title: Everyone Drives the G318 to Tibet. Drive the Duku Highway Instead | China Travel Expert
description:
The G318 to Tibet is China's most famous road trip. I'd skip it — and drive Xinjiang's Duku Highway instead. Fight me in the comments.

The G318 Sichuan–Tibet Highway runs 2,142 km from Chengdu to Lhasa, takes 10–12 days, tops out around 5,130 m, and — for foreign travellers — needs both a Tibet Travel Permit and an Alien's Travel Permit. It's a bucket-list drive, no argument. But the Duku Highway (G217's Dushanzi-to-Kuqa stretch) packs desert, red canyons, alpine meadows and snow into just 561 km across the Tianshan Mountains — "four seasons in one day" — with no Tibet permit required. The trade-off: the Duku is open only about four months a year, roughly June to early October, then the snow shuts it down.

🧭 Expert Tip: plan the Duku for June–September, start early from Dushanzi to clear the high passes before afternoon weather, and carry fuel and cash — services between towns are thin.
